key_insight: Halide ordering in mixed Cs/Rb lead halide perovskites strongly reshapes miscibility and structural phase transitions, especially in CsPbBr3yI3-3y where it can shift transition temperatures by up to 100 K.
engineering_relevance: Compositional and cation engineering can be used to tune phase stability and suppress unwanted structural changes in mixed-halide perovskite devices.
method: Trained machine-learned interatomic potentials on DFT reference data for three mixed-halide perovskite families.
Ran large-scale hybrid Monte Carlo–molecular dynamics simulations to sample both configurational and vibrational effects.
Mapped miscibility gaps and site-preference trends across temperature and composition.
evidence_signal: The study reports phase behavior from simulations across 200–500 K, finding miscibility gaps in all systems and layered halide ordering above the gap, with composition-dependent shifts in transition temperatures.
watch_item: The conclusions are based on modeled thermodynamics, so experimental validation is still needed for device-specific processing conditions and defect-rich films.
paper_title: Strong Impact of Halide Ordering on Structural Phase Transitions in Mixed Perovskites
